title: Competition review of The Clementi Mall acquisition and guidance on notifying mall mergers
asked: Mr David Hoe asked whether the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCS) has assessed the competition effects of The Clementi Mall acquisition on retail tenant mix and leasing terms in the Clementi catchment, and whether the Ministry will issue guidance on when such mall acquisitions must be notified to CCS for competition review.
response: Ms Low Yen Ling said tenancy mix and turnover in commercial developments are commercial decisions influenced by market factors. Singapore uses a voluntary merger notification regime, where merger parties self-assess and may approach CCS for pre-notification discussions or guidance, and CCS has published detailed guidance on when mergers may raise competition concerns. The parties to The Clementi Mall acquisition have not formally notified CCS for a merger assessment, and CCS will continue to monitor market developments and can step in if it obtains information suggesting potential competition issues.

key_points.point: Tenancy mix and turnover in commercial developments result from commercial decisions by property owners and tenants.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: tenancy mix and turnover in commercial developments are the result of commercial decisions made by both property owners and tenants.

key_points.point: Singapore adopts a voluntary merger notification regime to balance regulatory oversight with low compliance costs.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: Singapore adopts a voluntary merger notification regime to balance between effective regulatory oversight and keeping compliance costs low.

key_points.point: Merger parties are expected to self-assess whether their transaction may raise competition concerns.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: Merger parties are expected to self-assess whether their transaction may give rise to potential competition concerns.

key_points.point: CCS has published detailed guidance on when mergers may raise competition concerns.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: CCS has published detailed guidance on the circumstances under which mergers may raise competition concerns.

key_points.point: The parties to The Clementi Mall acquisition have not formally notified CCS for a merger assessment.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: The parties to the acquisition of The Clementi Mall have not formally notified CCS for a merger assessment.

key_points.point: CCS will continue to monitor market developments and is empowered to step in if it obtains information suggesting potential competition issues.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: CCS will continue to monitor market developments and is empowered to step in, if it obtains information suggesting that a merger may result in potential competition issues.

key_points.point: CCS uses the CCS Guidelines on the Substantive Assessment of Mergers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: it is the CCS Guidelines on the Substantive Assessment of Mergers.

key_points.point: CCS assesses competition effects based on facts and circumstances, not hearsay, uncertainty or projections.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: based on facts, based on circumstances. Certainly, not based on hearsay, uncertainty, projections and so on.

key_points.point: If a transaction results in substantially less competition that compromises consumer welfare, CCS will step in.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: if any transaction results in substantially less competition that compromises the consumer welfare, CCS will step in.

key_points.point: Members of the public, including residents, can provide qualitative and quantitative feedback directly to CCS.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
key_points.quote: members of the public, including his residents, can certainly provide feedback – qualitative as well as quantitative – to CCS directly.

key_points.point: Residents can call the CCS hotline at 1800 325 8282.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling

key_points.point: Residents can also report anti-competitive behaviour through the CCS website.
key_points.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling

left_open: Whether CCS has assessed the competition effects on retail tenant mix and leasing terms in the Clementi catchment
Whether the Ministry will issue guidance on when such mall acquisitions must be notified to CCS for competition review
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered non-price competition effects, the basis and forms of CCS intervention, and what information, including public feedback, triggers CCS action.
